advances: A finite arithmetic criterion for a specified witness under an integrality filter. The simultaneous character test is on the actual deletion kernel.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The canonical-lift theorem in accepted fact ba0f3db1bf4f62c6 preserves every anchored convex representation and recovers each Jensen function affinely on the lift. Thus for each $V\subseteq P$ and $p\in P$ one has $p\in\operatorname{conv}(V)$ if and only if $(p,g(p))$ belongs to the convex hull of the corresponding graph points. The forward implication follows by taking a representation and evaluating the recovered affine function, and the reverse implication is projection. Apply this equivalence to each deletion hull of $W$. The lifted deletion kernel misses $T_g$ exactly when each base in $P\cap K(W)$ has nonintegral height.

Integer features can be chosen because the extreme vectors of every anchored coefficient polytope are rational and give finitely many rational linear equations for the Jensen space. Choose a rational basis of their nullspace and clear denominators in each basis function.

A rational $g$ integral on $W$ induces $\chi([v])=\alpha\cdot v+\mathbb Z$ on $G_W$. It has finite image because the denominators of the finitely many rational coordinates of $\alpha$ have a common multiple. At a kernel base $p$ its value is nonzero exactly when $g(p)$ is nonintegral. Conversely, pull a finite-order character back to the free lattice $\Lambda$. Take rational representatives of its values on a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $\Lambda$. A rational linear functional on the rational span of that basis realizes those values, and extends rationally to $\mathbb Q^\ell$. With coefficient vector $\alpha$ this gives a rational Jensen function, integral at all $w\in W$ because the pulled-back character vanishes on $\Lambda_W$. Nonzero character values on all specified classes give precisely the required exclusion of the kernel points.

For any $p\in P\cap K(W)$, $p\in\operatorname{conv}(W)$, so a rational anchored convex representation from $W$ exists. Indeed its feasible coefficient polytope has rational defining constraints and a rational extreme point. Jensen affinity of each feature coordinate represents $A_p$ by the same coefficients, and clearing denominators gives a positive multiple of $A_p$ in $\Lambda_W$. Thus every tested class lies in the torsion subgroup of the finitely generated abelian group $G_W$. The structure theorem splits off a free summand. Each character of the finite torsion subgroup extends by zero on the free summand, and restriction preserves all tested values. This proves finiteness and shows that the criterion requires one character satisfying all the nonvanishing tests at once.
statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^k$ be finite and nonempty. A Jensen function on $P$ preserves every convex representation whose target is in $P$. For a rational Jensen function $g$ set $P_g=\{p\in P:g(p)\in\mathbb Z\}$ and $T_g=\{(p,g(p)):p\in P_g\}$. For nonempty $W\subseteq P$ put $K(W)=\bigcap_{w\in W}\operatorname{conv}(W\setminus\{w\})$, with $\operatorname{conv}(\varnothing)=\varnothing$.

Choose integer feature rows $A_p\in\mathbb Z^\ell$ for a basis of the rational Jensen space so that every rational Jensen function is $g(p)=\alpha\cdot A_p$ for $\alpha\in\mathbb Q^\ell$. For a fixed nonempty $W\subseteq P$, set $\Lambda=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{A_p:p\in P\}$, $\Lambda_W=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{A_w:w\in W\}$, and $G_W=\Lambda/\Lambda_W$. Some rational Jensen function integral on $W$ makes the lifted $W$ a Helly witness in its integral graph if and only if a finite-order character $G_W\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ is nonzero on every class $[A_p]$ with $p\in P\cap K(W)$. All these classes are torsion. In particular, one such class being zero rules out $W$ for all rational Jensen functions. Testing the simultaneous condition on the finite torsion subgroup is sufficient and necessary.
title: A character criterion for integral Jensen graph Helly witnesses
